per_question.question: What are the general eligibility criteria for CAP/DA services under NC Medicaid?
per_question.agent_answer:
## General CAP/DA eligibility criteria

CAP/DA is an NC Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services waiver for adults with disabilities who are age 18 or older and at risk of institutionalization. To receive waiver services, an individual must meet Medicaid long-term-care eligibility requirements. [Policy 3K-2 § 1.0](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

In general, the beneficiary must:

- Be enrolled in NC Medicaid; the eligibility category may impose service restrictions that make the beneficiary ineligible, and providers must verify eligibility each time a service is rendered. [Policy 3K-2 § 2.1.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- Need medically necessary services that are individualized and consistent with the person’s symptoms or confirmed diagnosis and needs, can be furnished safely, have no equally effective and more conservative or less costly statewide alternative, and are not primarily for the convenience of the beneficiary, caregiver, or provider. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- Meet the HCBS nursing-facility level of care determined by NC Medicaid, with institutional-level long-term-care support needs directly related to documented medical and functional-care needs, as assessed quarterly. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- Have a completed CAP assessment indicating a reasonable need for a CAP/DA HCBS service plan within 30 calendar days of the evaluation. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- Have a signed service plan authorizing one or more monthly waiver services to mitigate institutionalization through coordinated case management. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- Have a signed service plan for short-term installation of equipment, modification, or technology when needed to return to or remain in a primary private residence and prevent institutional placement; the installation or modification must be completed within three calendar months of service-plan approval. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- Be able to maintain health, safety, and well-being in a primary private residence or other approved location using formal and informal supports. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- Have paid care needs that can be maintained within the waiver’s average institutional cost, a primary physician to link and coordinate medical services, and an emergency back-up and disaster plan. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

These are general policy criteria and do not determine a particular person’s eligibility.

scores.explanation: The agent's answer accurately captures all key eligibility criteria from the evidence: NC Medicaid enrollment (§2.1.1), medical necessity requirements (§3.1), HCBS nursing facility level of care, completed CAP assessment, signed service plan, ability to maintain health/safety in community, cost within institutional average, primary physician, and emergency/disaster plan (§3.2.1). The answer also correctly identifies the program as serving adults 18+ at risk of institutionalization (§1.0). All claims are directly supported by the evidence blocks. The answer provides precise section-level citations (Policy 3K-2 §§ 1.0, 2.1.1, 3.1, 3.2.1) with URLs. The disclaimer at the end is appropriate. No hallucinations detected - every bullet point maps to specific evidence text. The answer is more detailed than the reference answer but remains accurate and well-grounded in the policy evidence.

Content:
Medicaid shall cover procedures, products, and services related to this policy when they are medically necessary, and:
the procedure, product, or service is individualized, specific, and consistent with symptoms or confirmed diagnosis of the illness or injury under treatment, and not in excess of the beneficiary's needs;
the procedure, product, or service can be safely furnished, and no equally effective and more conservative or less costly treatment is available statewide; and
the procedure, product, or service is furnished in a manner not primarily intended for the convenience of the beneficiary, the beneficiary's caretaker, or the provider.

Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

Content:
The Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA) is a Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waiver authorized under section1915(c) of the Social Security Act and complies with 42 CFR § 440.180, Home and community-based waiver services. This waiver program provides a cost-effective alternative to institutionalization for a beneficiary, in a specified target population, who is at risk for institutionalization if specialized waiver services were not available. These services allow this targeted individual to remain in or return to a home and community-based setting.
HCBS waivers are approved by Centers of Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) for a specified time. The waiver establishes the requirements for program administration and funding. Federal regulations for HCBS waivers are found in 42 CFR Part 441 Subpart G, Home and Community-Based Services: Waiver Requirements. NC Medicaid can renew or amend the waiver with the approval of CMS. CMS may exercise its authority to terminate the waiver when it believes the waiver is not operated properly. The CAP/DA HCBS (referred to as CAP/DA for the purpose of this policy) is a waiver that serves an adult with disabilities 18 years of age and older who is at risk of institutionalization. To receive services from this waiver program as listed on the service plan, the individual shall meet the Medicaid eligibility requirements for long-term care.
Pursuant to 42 CFR§ 431.10, NC Medicaid is the administrative authority of the waiver and outlines the policies and procedures governing the waiver. NC Medicaid appoints local entities to provide the day-to-day operation of the waiver to ensure the primary six waiver assurances are met.

per_question.question: What DME items are specifically NOT covered by NC Medicaid under the Orthotics and Prosthetics policy, and what general criteria must be met for coverage?
per_question.agent_answer:
## Specifically not covered

Under NC Medicaid Clinical Coverage Policy 5B, the following orthotic/prosthetic devices and supplies are specifically excluded:

- Items primarily for the beneficiary’s or caregiver’s comfort or convenience.  
- Backup items or duplicates kept at different locations.  
- Devices and supplies for nursing-facility residents.  
- Devices or supplies that another agency covers.  
- Equipment or supplies for a beneficiary receiving hospice care. [Policy 5B § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

More generally, Medicaid does not cover an item or service when the beneficiary does not meet the policy’s eligibility or coverage criteria, when it duplicates another provider’s item or service, or when it is experimental, investigational, or part of a clinical trial. [Policy 5B § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

## General coverage criteria

For coverage, the orthotic or prosthetic must be ordered by a physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner; be medically necessary to maintain or improve the beneficiary’s medical, physical, or functional level; and be appropriate for the noninstitutional settings where normal life activities occur. [Policy 5B § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

There also must be a documented face-to-face encounter with the ordering clinician concerning the primary reason for the item within six months before services begin, and the ordering clinician must review the beneficiary’s need at least annually. [Policy 5B § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

An orthotic must be needed to correct or prevent skeletal deformity, support or align movable body parts, or preserve or improve physical function. A prosthetic must replace function lost because a body part is permanently inoperative, absent, or malfunctioning, and be needed for mobility, daily care, or rehabilitation. [Policy 5B § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

Finally, the device must be a reasonable and medically necessary part of the treatment plan, fit the beneficiary’s diagnosis, condition, functional limitations, and symptoms, and be high quality with obtainable replacement parts. [Policy 5B § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

scores.explanation: The agent's answer accurately captures all key facts from the evidence: the five specific exclusions in §4.2.1 (comfort/convenience devices, backup/duplicate devices, nursing facility residents, items covered by another agency, hospice care recipients), the general exclusions in §4.1 (eligibility failure, criteria failure, duplication, experimental), and the coverage criteria from §3.1 and §3.2.1 (ordering requirements, medical necessity, face-to-face encounter, annual review, orthotic/prosthetic-specific criteria). All claims are directly supported by the evidence blocks. Citations are precise and section-level (§3.2.1, §4.1, §4.2.1). The answer is more detailed than the reference answer but contains no hallucinations and fully addresses the question.

[corpusSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:3.2.1
Title: 3.2.1 Specific criteria covered by Medicaid
Section: 3.2.1
Policy: 5B
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

Content:
Medicaid shall cover orthotics and prosthetics when the beneficiary meets all the following specific criteria:
they are ordered by a physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner;
they are medically necessary to maintain or improve a beneficiary's medical, physical or functional level, and appropriate for use in any noninstitutional setting in which normal life activities take place;
a documented face-to-face encounter with the beneficiary and the ordering physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner related to the primary reason the beneficiary requires orthotics and prosthetics has occurred no more than six (6) months prior to the initiation of orthotics and prosthetics; and
the beneficiary's need for orthotics and prosthetics is reviewed by the ordering physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner at least annually.
Medicaid covers orthotic and prosthetic services when they are medically necessary, and the beneficiary meets the specific coverage requirements for the device.
Orthotic devices are medically necessary when required to correct or prevent skeletal deformities, to support or align movable body parts, or to preserve or improve physical function.
Prosthetic devices are medically necessary as a replacement for all or part of the function of a permanently inoperative, absent, or malfunctioning body part. The beneficiary shall require the prosthesis for mobility, daily care, or rehabilitation purposes.
In addition, orthotic and prosthetic devices must be:
a reasonable and medically necessary part of the beneficiary's treatment plan;
consistent with the beneficiary's diagnosis and medical condition, particularly the functional limitations and symptoms exhibited by the beneficiary; and
of high quality, with replacement parts available and obtainable.
Medical doctors (MDs), doctors of osteopathic medicine (DOs), doctors of podiatric medicine (DPMs), physician assistants (PAs) and nurse practitioners (NPs) may provide certain orthotic and prosthetic devices when the devices are part of the beneficiary's current care and treatment. These professionals may provide devices as indicated in the Required Provider Certification column of Attachment B .
To be reimbursed for an orthotic or prosthetic device, the provider shall be enrolled as an appropriate board-certified provider for the specific device. Refer to Attachment B, which includes the Required Professional Certification for Orthotic and Prosthetic Devices.
For specific coverage requirements, refer to Subsection 5.3, Documenting Medical Necessity.

per_question.question: What are the entrance, continued service, and discharge criteria for outpatient behavioral health services in NC Medicaid?
per_question.agent_answer:
NC Medicaid Policy 8C requires that outpatient behavioral health services be medically necessary, individualized to the beneficiary’s symptoms or confirmed diagnosis, safely furnished, not exceed the beneficiary’s needs, and not be primarily for convenience. [Policy 8C § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment) The current policy is effective April 15, 2025; the most recent amendment revised telephonic-service language, not these entrance/continuing/discharge criteria. [Policy 8C Change Notice 2025-04-15](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

## Entrance criteria
**All** of these must be present for admission to outpatient treatment:

- A current DSM-5 diagnosis (or diagnosis under a subsequent edition). [Policy 8C § 3.2.1.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
- Behavioral, psychological, or biological dysfunction and functional impairment consistent with and associated with that diagnosis. [Policy 8C § 3.2.1.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
- If a higher level of care is indicated but unavailable, or the beneficiary refuses it, outpatient services may be provided until that care is available or to support participation in it. [Policy 8C § 3.2.1.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
- The beneficiary can develop skills to manage symptoms, make behavioral changes, and respond favorably to therapeutic interventions. [Policy 8C § 3.2.1.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
- There is no evidence that an alternative intervention would be more effective under North Carolina community-practice standards. [Policy 8C § 3.2.1.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

## Continued-service criteria
To continue services, the beneficiary must meet **both** of these two prongs:

1. **One** of the following:
   - The desired outcome or functioning level has not been restored, improved, or sustained within the timeframe in the treatment plan;
   - The beneficiary remains at risk of relapse based on current clinical assessment and history; **or**
   - The functional gains are tenuous. [Policy 8C § 3.2.1.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

**And**

2. **One** of the following:
   - The beneficiary has met current treatment-plan goals but has additional goals indicated by documented symptoms; **or**
   - The beneficiary is making satisfactory progress toward goals, with documentation supporting that continued service is expected to effectively address the treatment-plan goals. [Policy 8C § 3.2.1.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

## Discharge criteria
Discharge is appropriate when **any one** of these applies:

- The beneficiary’s functioning has improved in relation to the treatment-plan goals;
- The beneficiary or legally responsible person no longer wants the services; **or**
- Despite treatment-plan modifications, the beneficiary has not improved and needs a more appropriate best-practice or evidence-based treatment modality under North Carolina community-practice standards. [Policy 8C § 3.2.1.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

A treatment plan is required within 15 business days after the first face-to-face contact, must be assessment-based and developed with the beneficiary or legally responsible person, and must be reviewed at least annually; this documentation is important for applying the continued-service and discharge standards. [Policy 8C § 7.3.4](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

[corpusSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:7.4
Title: 7.4 24-Hour Coverage for Behavioral Health Crises
Section: 7.4
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-15
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
Enrolled providers shall provide, or have a written agreement with another entity, for access to 24-hour coverage for behavioral health emergency services. Enrolled providers shall arrange for coverage in the event that they are not available to respond to a beneficiary in crisis. This coverage must incorporate the ability for the beneficiary to speak with the licensed clinician on call either in-person, via telehealth, or telephonically.

Title: 4.2.1.1 Outpatient Behavioral Health
Section: 4.2.1.1
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-15
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
Medicaid shall not cover Outpatient Behavioral Health Services for the following:
sleep therapy for psychiatric disorders;
when services are not provided in-person or in accordance with Attachment A;
when a beneficiary presents with a medical, cognitive, intellectual or development issue that would not benefit from outpatient treatment services;
when the focus of treatment does not address the symptoms of the diagnosis;
when the requirements and limitations in Section 5.0 are not followed; and
when Psychotherapy for Crisis codes are billed, the same provider shall not bill Special Services: After Hours codes. Refer to clinical coverage policy 1A-38, Special Services: After Hours, located on NC Medicaid's website at https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/, for the same event.

[corpusSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.4
Title: 3.2.4 Best Practice or Evidence-Based Practice
Section: 3.2.4
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-15
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
Outpatient behavioral health service providers and those providing Psychotherapy for Crisis and psychological testing, shall be trained in and follow a rehabilitative best practice or evidence-based treatment model consistent with NC community practice standards. The treatment model must be expected to produce positive outcomes for the population being treated. The treatment model must address the clinical needs of the beneficiary identified in the comprehensive clinical assessment and on any subsequent assessments. Qualified interpreters shall be used, if necessary, to deliver test instructions in the examinee's preferred language.
Refer to Section 5.0 for additional requirements and limitations.

Policy: 8C

Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
Medicaid shall cover procedures, products, and services related to this policy when they are medically necessary, and:
the procedure, product, or service is individualized, specific, and consistent with symptoms or confirmed diagnosis of the illness or injury under treatment, and not in excess of the beneficiary's needs;
the procedure, product, or service can be safely furnished, and no equally effective and more conservative or less costly treatment is available statewide; and
the procedure, product, or service is furnished in a manner not primarily intended for the convenience of the beneficiary, the beneficiary's caretaker, or the provider.

Content:
Medicaid shall cover outpatient behavioral health services when the beneficiary meets the following criteria:

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.1
Title: 3.2.1.1 Entrance Criteria
Section: 3.2.1.1
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-15
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
All of the following criteria are necessary for admission of a beneficiary to outpatient treatment services:
A current Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition [(DSM-5) or any subsequent editions of this reference material] diagnosis;
The beneficiary presents behavioral, psychological, or biological dysfunction and functional impairment, which are consistent and associated with the current diagnosis;
If a higher level of care is indicated but unavailable or the beneficiary is refusing the service, outpatient services can be provided until the appropriate level of care is available or to support the beneficiary to participate in that higher level of care;
The beneficiary is capable of developing skills to manage symptoms, make behavioral changes, and respond favorably to therapeutic interventions;
There is no evidence to support that alternative interventions would be more effective, based on North Carolina community practice standards (Best Practice Guidelines of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, American Psychiatric Association, American Board of Addiction Medicine)

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.2
Title: 3.2.1.2 Continued Service Criteria
Section: 3.2.1.2
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-15
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
The criteria for continued service must meet both 'a.' and 'b.' below:
Any ONE of the following criteria:
The desired outcome or level of functioning has not been restored, improved, or sustained over the timeframe outlined in the beneficiary's treatment plan;
The beneficiary continues to be at risk for relapse based on current clinical assessment, and history: or
Tenuous nature of the functional gains.
Any ONE of the following criteria (in addition to 'a.')
The beneficiary has achieved current treatment plan goals, and additional goals are indicated as evidenced by documented symptoms; or
The beneficiary is making satisfactory progress toward meeting goals and there is documentation that supports that
continuation of this service is expected to be effective in addressing the goals outlined in the treatment plan.

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.3
Title: 3.2.1.3 Discharge Criteria
Section: 3.2.1.3
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-15
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
Any ONE of the following criteria must be met:
The beneficiary's level of functioning has improved with respect to the goals outlined in the treatment plan;
The beneficiary or legally responsible person no longer wishes to receive these services; or
The beneficiary, based on presentation and failure to show improvement, despite modifications in the treatment plan, requires a more appropriate best practice or evidence-based treatment modality based on North Carolina community practice standards (National Institute of Drug Abuse, American Psychiatric Association).

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:7.3.4
Title: 7.3.4 Individualized Plan
Section: 7.3.4
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-15
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
An individualized plan of care, service plan, treatment plan, or PCP, referred to as 'plan,' consistent with and supportive of the service provided and within professional standards of practice, is required within 15 business days of the first face-to-face beneficiary contact. This plan is based on the assessment and is developed in partnership with the beneficiary or legally responsible person, or both. When services are provided prior to the establishment and implementation of the plan, strategies to address the beneficiary's presenting problem must be documented. The plan must be an identifiable document in the service record.
The plan must contain at a minimum:
beneficiary outcomes that are anticipated to be achieved by provision of the service and a projected date of achievement;
strategies;
staff responsible;
a schedule for review of the plan (in consultation with the beneficiary or legally responsible person or both) as needed but at least annually to review goals and strategies to promote effective treatment;
basis for evaluation or assessment of outcome achievement; and
written consent or agreement by the beneficiary or legally responsible person, or a written statement by the provider stating why such consent could not be obtained.
For a child or adolescent receiving outpatient substance use services, the plan must document both the staff and the child or adolescent's signatures demonstrating the involvement of all responsible parties in the development of the plan and the child or adolescent's consent or agreement to the plan. Consistent with N.C.G.S. § 90-21.5 or comparable federal, Tribal law, or rule, the plan may be implemented without parental consent when services are provided under the direction and supervision of a physician. When services are not provided under the direction and supervision of a physician, the plan must require the signature of the parent or legally responsible person for the child or adolescent demonstrating the involvement of the parent or legally responsible person in the development of the plan and the parent's or legally responsible person's consent to the plan.
The treatment plan must be updated as required, but a new plan is required at least annually.
All treatment plans must be developed in partnership with the beneficiary or legally responsible person, and all updated or new plans require the beneficiary or legally responsible person's signature, and the licensed professional's signature. The licensed professional's signature on the updated or new plan can serve as the service order.
Note: Beneficiaries receiving medication management only would be exempt from the requirement of having to sign the treatment plan. For beneficiaries receiving medication management only and who have a legally responsible person, the legally responsible person would also be exempt from this requirement. Refer to Attachment A, Section C for E/M code documentation requirements. The treatment plan for beneficiaries receiving only medication management would not need to be a separate document and could be integrated into service notes.

per_question.question: How does the EPSDT special provision affect coverage for outpatient therapy services, and what ordering practitioner requirements apply to beneficiaries under 21?
per_question.agent_answer:
## EPSDT effect on outpatient therapy coverage

For a beneficiary under 21, EPSDT can allow outpatient specialized-therapy limits—such as limits on scope, amount, duration, frequency, service location, or other policy criteria—to be exceeded or not applied when documentation establishes that the therapy is medically necessary to correct or ameliorate a condition found through a screening or evaluation. The documentation must show how the requested service will correct, improve, or maintain health; compensate for the problem; prevent worsening; or prevent additional health problems. EPSDT does not require coverage of services that are unsafe, ineffective, experimental/investigational, nonmedical, or not generally accepted medical practice. [Policy 10A § 2.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

This is an exception to policy limitations, not an automatic entitlement to therapy. [Policy 10A § 2.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment) For example, outpatient speech-language treatment remains subject to medical-necessity requirements, and speech-language therapy requires prior authorization. [Policy 10A § 3.2.1.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment) Audiology/aural-rehabilitation therapy also requires the applicable hearing-loss or auditory-processing findings and measurable functional limitations. [Policy 10A § 3.2.1.4](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

Being under 21 does **not** waive prior approval. Prior approval is required before treatment starts for beneficiaries under 21, and the request must include support that EPSDT criteria are met and evidence-based literature, if available. [Policy 10A § 5.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment) [Policy 10A § b. EPSDT and Prior Approval Requirements](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

## Ordering-practitioner requirement

Outpatient specialized-therapy services must be ordered by an **NC Medicaid-enrolled** MD, DO, DPM, certified nurse midwife, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner. [Policy 10A § 3.1.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

Home-health outpatient specialized therapies may instead be ordered under the practitioner provisions of Clinical Coverage Policy 3A, as specified by Policy 10A. [Policy 10A § 3.1.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

scores.explanation: The agent's answer accurately covers all key aspects: EPSDT provision allowing policy limitations to be exceeded for under-21 beneficiaries when medically necessary (§2.2.1), the ordering practitioner requirements listing MD/DO/DPM/CNM/PA/NP (§3.1.2), prior approval requirements not being waived by EPSDT status (§b and §5.2), speech-language therapy criteria (§3.2.1.3), and audiology/aural rehabilitation criteria (§3.2.1.4). All claims are supported by the evidence blocks. Citations are precise and section-level. The answer correctly notes EPSDT exclusions (unsafe, experimental, non-medical services), the home health ordering practitioner exception referencing Policy 3A, and the requirement to submit EPSDT criteria support with prior approval requests. No hallucinations detected - every factual claim maps to the evidence provided.

[corpusSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:10A:2.2.1
Title: 2.2.1 EPSDT Special Provision: Exception to Policy Limitations for a Medicaid Beneficiary under 21 Years of Age
Section: 2.2.1
Policy: 10A
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-02-01
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

Content:
42 U.S.C. § 1396d(r) [1905(r) of the Social Security Act]
Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) is a federal Medicaid requirement that requires the state Medicaid agency to cover services, products, or procedures for Medicaid beneficiary under 21 years of age if the service is medically necessary health care to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition [health problem] identified through a screening examination ** (includes any evaluation by a physician or other licensed clinician).
This means EPSDT covers most of the medical or remedial care a child needs to improve or maintain his or her health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.
Medically necessary services will be provided in the most economic mode, as long as the treatment made available is similarly efficacious to the service requested by the beneficiary's physician, therapist, or other licensed practitioner; the determination process does not delay the delivery of the needed service; and the determination does not limit the beneficiary's right to a free choice of providers.
EPSDT does not require the state Medicaid agency to provide any service, product or procedure:
that is unsafe, ineffective, or experimental or investigational.
that is not medical in nature or not generally recognized as an accepted method of medical practice or treatment.
Service limitations on scope, amount, duration, frequency, location of service, and other specific criteria described in clinical coverage policies may be exceeded or may not apply as long as the provider's documentation shows that the requested service is medically necessary 'to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition' [health problem]; that is, provider documentation shows how the service, product, or procedure meets all EPSDT criteria, including to correct or improve or maintain the beneficiary's health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:10A:2.2.1
Title: 2.2.1 EPSDT Special Provision: Exception to Policy Limitations for a Medicaid Beneficiary under 21 Years of Age
Section: 2.2.1
Policy: 10A
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-02-01
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

Content:
42 U.S.C. § 1396d(r) [1905(r) of the Social Security Act]
Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) is a federal Medicaid requirement that requires the state Medicaid agency to cover services, products, or procedures for Medicaid beneficiary under 21 years of age if the service is medically necessary health care to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition [health problem] identified through a screening examination ** (includes any evaluation by a physician or other licensed clinician).
This means EPSDT covers most of the medical or remedial care a child needs to improve or maintain his or her health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.
Medically necessary services will be provided in the most economic mode, as long as the treatment made available is similarly efficacious to the service requested by the beneficiary's physician, therapist, or other licensed practitioner; the determination process does not delay the delivery of the needed service; and the determination does not limit the beneficiary's right to a free choice of providers.
EPSDT does not require the state Medicaid agency to provide any service, product or procedure:
that is unsafe, ineffective, or experimental or investigational.
that is not medical in nature or not generally recognized as an accepted method of medical practice or treatment.
Service limitations on scope, amount, duration, frequency, location of service, and other specific criteria described in clinical coverage policies may be exceeded or may not apply as long as the provider's documentation shows that the requested service is medically necessary 'to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition' [health problem]; that is, provider documentation shows how the service, product, or procedure meets all EPSDT criteria, including to correct or improve or maintain the beneficiary's health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.

per_question.question: Does NC Medicaid cover Personal Care Services for beneficiaries who live in an assisted living facility?
per_question.agent_answer:
**Yes—NC Medicaid can cover Personal Care Services (PCS) for a beneficiary living in an assisted living facility, if the facility is a North Carolina-licensed Adult Care Home and the beneficiary meets the policy’s eligibility and service criteria.** PCS in congregate settings is provided by paraprofessional aides employed by licensed home-care agencies, licensed Adult Care Homes, or licensed supervised-living-home staff. [Policy 3L-1 § 1.0](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

Among other requirements, the beneficiary must have qualifying unmet needs for specified activities of daily living, reside in an eligible licensed congregate setting, have no other payer responsible for the service, lack an available/willing/able informal caregiver for the authorized times, be under ongoing physician care for the condition causing the functional limitation, and be medically stable without needing continuous licensed-nurse care, monitoring, or supervision. [Policy 3L-1 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

Coverage is not available if the person does not meet the policy’s eligibility or coverage criteria, if the service duplicates another provider’s service, or if it is experimental, investigational, or part of a clinical trial. [Policy 3L-1 § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment) It also is not covered, for example, when required assessments or authorization are missing, services exceed the approved amount, services occur outside the beneficiary’s primary congregate residence, or an available informal caregiver can regularly meet the personal-care need. [Policy 3L-1 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

It correctly identifies Policy 3L-1 as the governing policy for PCS in congregate settings, accurately describes the eligibility criteria from Section 3.2.1 (ADL requirements, facility type, physician care, medical stability, no informal caregiver, no third-party payer), correctly notes non-coverage conditions from Sections 4.1 and 4.2.1, and all claims are supported by the evidence provided. The answer cites specific policy sections (3L-1 §1.0, §3.2.1, §4.1, §4.2.1) with links. No hallucinations are present. The answer matches the reference answer's key points about the congregate-setting policy governing assisted living PCS coverage.

[corpusSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:3.2.1
Title: 3.2.1 Specific criteria covered by Medicaid
Section: 3.2.1
Policy: 3L-1
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

Content:
Medicaid shall cover State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings when the beneficiary meets the following specific criteria and other items in this section:
has a medical or mental condition, disability, or cognitive impairment and demonstrates unmet needs for, at a minimum:
three of the five qualifying activities of daily living (ADLs) with limited hands-on assistance. Refer to Subsection 5.4.3;
two ADLs, one of which requires extensive assistance; or
two ADLs, one of which requires assistance at the full dependence level.
resides in:
a congregate facility licensed by the State of North Carolina as an Adult Care Home (ACH) as defined in NC G.S. §131D-2.1, a combination home as defined in NC G.S. § 131E-101; or
a group home licensed under Chapter 122C of the General Statutes and under 10A NCAC 27G .5601 (b)(2) as a supervised living facility for two or more adults whose primary diagnosis is mental illness, a developmental disability, or substance abuse dependency and is eligible to receive personal care services under the Medicaid State Plan.
In addition to the specific criteria in Subsection 3.2.1 a and b of this policy, the following criteria must be met:
The congregate setting is safe and free of health hazards for the beneficiary and PCS provider(s), as determined by a facility environmental assessment conducted by NC Medicaid or a DHHS designated contractor;
The congregate setting has received inspection conducted by the Division of Health Service Regulation (DHSR)
The place of service is safe for the beneficiary to receive PCS and for an aide to provide PCS;
No other third-party payer is responsible for covering PCS;
No family or household member or other informal caregiver is available, willing, and able to provide the authorized services during those periods of time when the services are provided;
The required PCS are directly linked to a documented medical or mental condition or physical or cognitive impairment causing the functional limitations requiring the PCS;
The beneficiary is under the ongoing direct care of a physician for the medical condition or diagnosis causing the functional limitations; and
The beneficiary is medically stable and does not require continuous care, monitoring (precautionary observation), or supervision (observation resulting in an intervention) by a licensed nurse or other licensed health care professional; and
Screening for Serious Mental Illness (SMI) in Adult Care Homes licensed under G.S. §131D-2.4 Effective November 1, 2018, any Medicaid beneficiary referred to or seeking admission to Adult Care Homes licensed under G.S. 131D-2.4 must be referred to a Tailored Plan Transition Coordinator for the Referral Screening Verification Process. Adult Care Home providers licensed under G.S. § 131D-2.4 shall not receive a PCS assessment or prior approval without verification of a Referral Screening ID.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:4.2
Title: 4.2 Specific Criteria Not Covered
Section: 4.2
Policy: 3L-1
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

Content:
[Container heading with 2 child sections:]

### 4.2.1 Medicaid Additional Criteria Not Covered
Medicaid shall not cover Personal Care Services in Congregate Settings when:
the initial independent assessment has not been completed;
the PCS is not documented as completed according to this clinical coverage policy;
a reassessment has not been completed within 30 calendar days of the end date of the previous prior authorization period because the beneficiary refused the assessment, could not be reached to schedule the assessment, or did not attend the scheduled assessment;
Note: A delayed scheduling of a reassessment due to the Comprehensive Independent Assessment Entity (CIAE) timeline must not impact the continuous coverage of PCS while the reassessment is being arranged.
the PCS is provided at a location other than the beneficiary's primary congregate living setting;
the PCS exceeds the amount approved by the Comprehensive Independent Assessment Entity (CIAE);
the PCS is not completed on the date the service is billed;
the PCS is provided prior to the effective date or after the end date of the prior authorized service period;
the PCS is performed by an individual who is the beneficiary's legally responsible person, spouse, child, parent, sibling, grandparent, grandchild, or equivalent step or in-law relationship to the beneficiary;
Clinical Coverage Policy No: 3L-1
Amended Date:
family members or other informal caregivers are willing, able, and available on a regular basis adequate to meet the beneficiary's need for personal care; or
independent medical information does not validate the assessment, PCS hours may be reduced, denied, or terminated based on the additional information.
Note
: Adult Care Home Providers are not subject to the EVV requirement.

### 4.2.2 Medicaid Additional Criteria Not Covered
Medicaid shall not cover PCS when rendered concurrently with another substantially equivalent Federal or State funded service. Services equivalent to PCS are:
home health aide services and in-home aide services in the Community Alternatives Programs (CAP/Choice, CAP/Disabled Adults); and
Private Duty Nursing (PDN).

per_question.question: Does NC Medicaid cover chiropractic services under Clinical Coverage Policy 5B?
per_question.agent_answer:
**No.** Clinical Coverage Policy 5B does not cover chiropractic services; it governs **orthotic and prosthetic devices**, not chiropractic treatment. The policy covers those devices when prescribed by the treating physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner and when medical necessity is documented. [Policy 5B § 1.0](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

Its general exclusions also apply only to the procedure, product, or service governed by Policy 5B, including when coverage criteria are unmet, the service duplicates another provider’s service, or it is experimental or investigational. [Policy 5B § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

scores.explanation: The agent correctly answers 'No' and accurately identifies that Policy 5B covers orthotic and prosthetic devices, not chiropractic services. All claims are supported by the evidence: Section 1.0 confirms the policy scope (orthotics/prosthetics prescribed by treating physicians with documented medical necessity), and Section 4.1 confirms the general exclusion criteria cited. The agent provides precise section-level citations (§1.0 and §4.1) with URLs matching the evidence. No hallucinated facts are present. The answer is complete and would be accepted by a Medicaid policy expert.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:1.0
Title: 1.0 Description of the Procedure, Product, or Service
Section: 1.0
Policy: 5B
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

Content:
Orthotic and prosthetic devices are covered by NC Medicaid (Medicaid) when they are prescribed by the beneficiary's treating physician, physician's assistant, or nurse practitioner and medical necessity is documented. An orthotic or prosthetic device is medically necessary if it is needed to maintain or improve a beneficiary's medical, physical, or functional level.
Covered orthotic and prosthetic devices become the property of the beneficiary.
Refer to Attachment B for a list of HCPCS codes, established lifetime expectancies, quantity limitations, and required provider certification for Orthotics and Prosthetics.
For the rates associated with the list of HCPCS codes found in Attachment B, refer to the Orthotics and Prosthetics fee schedule at https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/providers.
In compliance with the CMS Home Health Final Rule Title 42, §440.70, items not listed in Attachment B or in the Orthotics and Prosthetics fee schedule may be considered for coverage if requested by a provider, or a beneficiary through a provider, and submitted for prior authorization (PA) review of medical necessity. For beneficiaries under age 21, please request an 'EPSDT review' using NCTracks. Refer to section 2.2 Special Provisions for more information about EPSDT. For beneficiaries aged 21 and older, please submit the request through NCTracks per the procedure detailed in Attachment E: Requesting Unlisted Orthotics and Prosthetics for Adults .

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:1.0
Title: 1.0 Description of the Procedure, Product, or Service
Section: 1.0
Policy: 5B
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

Content:
Orthotic and prosthetic devices are covered by NC Medicaid (Medicaid) when they are prescribed by the beneficiary's treating physician, physician's assistant, or nurse practitioner and medical necessity is documented. An orthotic or prosthetic device is medically necessary if it is needed to maintain or improve a beneficiary's medical, physical, or functional level.
Covered orthotic and prosthetic devices become the property of the beneficiary.
Refer to Attachment B for a list of HCPCS codes, established lifetime expectancies, quantity limitations, and required provider certification for Orthotics and Prosthetics.
For the rates associated with the list of HCPCS codes found in Attachment B, refer to the Orthotics and Prosthetics fee schedule at https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/providers.
In compliance with the CMS Home Health Final Rule Title 42, §440.70, items not listed in Attachment B or in the Orthotics and Prosthetics fee schedule may be considered for coverage if requested by a provider, or a beneficiary through a provider, and submitted for prior authorization (PA) review of medical necessity. For beneficiaries under age 21, please request an 'EPSDT review' using NCTracks. Refer to section 2.2 Special Provisions for more information about EPSDT. For beneficiaries aged 21 and older, please submit the request through NCTracks per the procedure detailed in Attachment E: Requesting Unlisted Orthotics and Prosthetics for Adults .

Medicaid shall not cover the procedure, product, or service related to this policy when:
the beneficiary does not meet the eligibility requirements listed in Section 2.0;
the beneficiary does not meet the criteria listed in Section 3.0;
the procedure, product, or service duplicates another provider's procedure, product, or service; or

[corpusSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:10A:_s36
Title: Treatment services must adhere to the following requirements:
Policy: 10A
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-02-01
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

Content:
A verbal or a written order must be obtained for services prior to the start of services. All verbal orders must report the date and signature of the person receiving the order, must be recorded in the beneficiary's health record and shall be countersigned by the physician within 60 calendar days. All verbal orders are valid up to six months from the documented date of receipt . All written orders are valid up to six months from the date of the physician's signature. Backdating is not allowed.
All services must be provided according to a treatment plan that meets the requirements in Subsection 3.2.1.6.
Service providers shall review and renew or revise treatment plans and goals at least every six calendar months.
Prior approval is required prior to the start of treatment services.
For a Local Education Agency (LEA), the prior approval process is deemed met by the Individualized Education Program (IEP), Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP), Individual Health Plan (IHP), Behavior Intervention Plan (BIP), or 504 Plan processes. An LEA provider shall review, renew and revise the IEP, IFSP, IHP, BIP or 504 Plan annually along with obtaining a dated physician order with signature. The requirement of parent notification must occur at regular intervals throughout the year as stipulated by NC Department of Public Instruction. Such notification must detail how progress is sufficient to enable the child to achieve the goals by the end of the school year.
Faxed orders and faxed signatures are permissible and serve the same purposes for documentation as an original signature on an original form or order sheet. Electronic signatures and printed dates are acceptable. Providers using electronic signatures shall maintain policies regarding the use of electronic documentation addressing the security of records and the unique signature, sanctions against improper or unauthorized use, and reconstruction of records in the event of a system breakdown. Stamped signatures are not permitted.
Instructional training of the beneficiary, parent(s) or legal guardian(s) that incorporates activities and strategies to target the goals and facilitate progress must be considered when appropriate for the therapeutic place of service.

[corpusSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:10A:5.1
Title: 5.1 Prior Approval
Section: 5.1
Policy: 10A
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-02-01
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

Content:
Medicaid shall require prior approval for Outpatient Specialized Therapies. The provider shall obtain prior approval before rendering Outpatient Specialized Therapies.
Note: Refer to Subsections 3.2.1.5, 5.1.2, and 5.2 for prior authorization exclusions.
To obtain prior approval, the request must clearly indicate that the service of a licensed therapist is required. Retroactive prior approval is considered when a beneficiary does not have Medicaid coverage at the time of the procedure and is later approved for Medicaid with a retroactive eligibility date. Medicaid does not guarantee approval of retroactive requests.

Medicaid shall cover medically necessary outpatient physical therapy treatment for a beneficiary when prior authorization is received. Refer to Section 5.0 .

per_question.question: Can a CAP/DA beneficiary transfer between service providers, and what rules govern transfers of eligible beneficiaries?
per_question.agent_answer:
## Yes — a CAP/DA beneficiary may change service providers, and an eligible beneficiary may transfer to another county or entity.

### Governing rule

A beneficiary who is Medicaid-eligible may seek care from any willing, qualified service provider, and CAP/DA policy specifically requires the Case Management Entity (CME) to obtain the beneficiary’s or responsible party’s signed freedom-of-choice form when there is a change in provider agency. [Policy 3K-2 § 5.4.5](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

For a provider-agency change, the policy says the plan of care (POC) must be updated; it characterizes that agency-change update as not itself being a service-plan “revision.” [Policy 3K-2 § 5.4.5](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) Separately, the policy states that a POC revision is required when there is a change in a service provider, with the CME designee responsible for revisions caused by a change in the beneficiary’s needs. [Policy 3K-2 § 5.4.5](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

### Transfer of an eligible CAP/DA beneficiary

When the CME receives a transfer request, it must coordinate a transfer to another county or entity by the agreed transition date or within 30 calendar days of the request. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

The CME must coordinate the transfer to avoid gaps in service and, before transfer, determine the expected service-start date; coordinate a transition plan between provider agencies; plan for the beneficiary’s health, safety, and well-being; transfer the electronic health record through the CAP Business System; arrange a receiving-entity home visit within five business days after the move to the new primary residence; and arrange for services to begin on the first day of transfer. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

For a county-to-county transfer, the transferring and receiving CMEs must coordinate with each other, discuss health, safety, and well-being, transfer the electronic record, and ensure services begin on the transfer date. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

An active CAP/DA participant remains eligible to participate after moving to another county; the policy says eligibility for CAP/DA continues regardless of county of residence, although ongoing Medicaid eligibility is determined at the next Medicaid certification period. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) If the originating county has a waitlist, the transferring beneficiary is in a priority category and is guaranteed a slot immediately in the receiving county. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

### Current-policy note

This is the current Policy 3K-2 version effective September 1, 2025. [Policy 3K-2 Change Notice All sections and attachments](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) The September 2025 amendment made a limited wording change to § 3.3(b), adding “birth” to “month”; it did not identify a substantive change to the general transfer procedure described above. [Policy 3K-2 Change Notice 4](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

It correctly identifies Policy 3K-2 § 3.3 as governing transfers, accurately describes the 30-calendar-day timeline, the CME's coordination responsibilities, the steps required before transfer (home visit within 5 business days, electronic health record transfer, service start on first day of transfer), county-to-county transfer procedures, eligibility continuity regardless of county, and the priority category status for transferring beneficiaries. It also correctly covers provider agency changes under § 5.4.5 and the freedom-of-choice requirement. The amendment note about § 3.3(b) adding 'birth' to 'month' is supported by the evidence. All claims are grounded in the evidence blocks provided, with no hallucinations detected. Citations are precise and section-level throughout.

Medicaid shall not cover the procedure, product, or service related to this policy when:
the beneficiary does not meet the eligibility requirements listed in Section 2.0;
the beneficiary does not meet the criteria listed in Section 3.0;
the procedure, product, or service duplicates another provider's procedure, product, or service; or
the procedure, product, or service is experimental, investigational, or part of a clinical trial.

Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

Content:
Medicaid shall cover procedures, products, and services related to this policy when they are medically necessary, and:
the procedure, product, or service is individualized, specific, and consistent with symptoms or confirmed diagnosis of the illness or injury under treatment, and not in excess of the beneficiary's needs;
the procedure, product, or service can be safely furnished, and no equally effective and more conservative or less costly treatment is available statewide; and
the procedure, product, or service is furnished in a manner not primarily intended for the convenience of the beneficiary, the beneficiary's caretaker, or the provider.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.3
Title: 3.3 Transfers of Eligible Beneficiaries
Section: 3.3
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-09-01
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

Content:
When a transfer request is received, by the Case Management Entity (CME), the CME shall coordinate the transfer of an eligible CAP/DA beneficiary to another county or entity within the approved, agreed upon transition date or less than 30 calendar days of the request to transfer.
CME shall coordinate the transfer to prevent gaps in service provisions. The following steps must be completed prior to the transfer:
determine anticipated start date of service;
coordinate transition plan between provider agencies;
discuss and plan for the health, safety and well-being of the beneficiary;
initiate in the CAP Business System (e-CAP/DA) the transfer of the electronic health records to the receiving county;
arrange for a home visit within five (5) business days of the date the CAP/DA beneficiary moves to their new primary residence by the receiving entity to assess the home environment identifying any health and welfare concerns and planning for mitigation and safety; and
coordinate and plan the provision of services to start on the first date of the transfer.
For a CAP/C beneficiary aging out of CAP/C and wishes to transfer to CAP/DA:
The CAP/C CME designee shall implement a transition, transfer plan 12 months prior to the birth month. These coordination activities are:
Completion of a transition plan during the annual needs review assessment that occurs at age 20; and
Consultation with the CAP/C beneficiary and primary caregiver to educate about other Medicaid and community resources to meet needs after the age of 21.
Three months (90 calendar days) prior to the birth month or identified transfer month, a multidisciplinary team meeting must be convened to discuss care needs and to ensure the identified formal and informal resources are able to meet care needs.
The month prior to the birth month, the local DSS must be notified of the need to change the CAP evidence code for CAP/DA participation for the identified CAP/DA effective start date.
On the first day of the birth month or identified transfer month, CAP/DA services are authorized and provided to the beneficiary.
Note: A Service Request Form (SFR) is not required. An assessment is required to identify ongoing adult needs for the generation of an adult service plan.
For a CAP/DA beneficiary transferring to a different county:
The CME designee of the transferring agency shall coordinate the transfer with the CME designee of the receiving agency upon the agreed upon transfer date or less than 30 calendar days of the request to transfer.
The CME designee of the transferring and receiving agencies shall discuss and plan for the health, safety and well-being of the beneficiary.
The electronic health record is transferred to the receiving county.
The CME designee of the receiving agency shall arrange for a home visit within five (5) business days of the date the CAP/DA beneficiary moves in their new primary residence to assess the environment to identify any health and welfare concerns to plan for mitigation and safety.
The CME designee shall coordinate and plan the provision of services to start on the first date of the transfer into the receiving county.
Note: An active beneficiary previously approved to participate in CAP/DA can continue to participate in the program when a transfer to another county occurs. A transferring beneficiary continues to be eligible for CAP/DA regardless of their county of residence.  Ongoing Medicaid eligibility is determined at the next Medicaid certification period.
When a waitlist is active in the transferring county, the CAP/DA beneficiary is considered in a priority category and guaranteed a slot immediately in the receiving county.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:6.5
Title: 6.5 Medicaid Provider Requirement to Provide CAP/DA Waiver Services
Section: 6.5
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-09-01
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

Content:
Qualified NC Medicaid providers are granted approval to render CAP services through a managed change request.  Providers are approved based on their approved Medicaid provider application and their qualifying taxonomies. Each qualified provider must adhere to the following when selected to render a CAP/DA service:
register as a user of the CAP Business System (e-CAP) and participate in required trainings.
accept, decline, or acknowledge service authorizations within three (3) business days of submission in the e-CAP system.
complete a CAP/DA overview and orientation training prior to rendering authorized services, and annually thereafter for updates and refresher of CAP/DA policies.
attest to having policies and procedures that identifies the assurance of nonuse of restraints and seclusions and critical incident management.
attest that hired workers successfully pass a background check that includes a health care registry.
comply with Section 12006 1903(l) of the 21st Century Cures Act and any subsequent amendments, when applicable.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:5.4.5
Title: 5.4.5 Changes and Revision to the Service Plan
Section: 5.4.5
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-09-01
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

Content:
A plan of care (POC) revision is required when a request is made to add, reduce, increase, delete a CAP/DA service or Medicaid State service, or when there are changes in a service provider. The Case Management Entity (CME) designee is responsible for revising the POC when there is a change in the beneficiary's needs.
Service plan revisions are approved by unbiased personnel within the CME. Revisions for an urgent need because of a critical change in status may be approved retroactively for up to 30 calendar days prior to the date that the plan is revised. The beneficiary or the primary caregiver shall agree to and sign and date the service plan acknowledging changes for CAP/DA provisions.
Note : Specified plan of care revisions may require a minor change to the approval without the legal guardian or the primary caregiver's signature. The eCAP Business System provides guidance in that area.
Service plan revisions, excluding goods and services, training, education, and consultative services, home and vehicle modifications and assistive technology, may be approved retroactively for up to 30 calendar days, when an urgent need is identified that places the CAP/DA beneficiary at risk of losing their community placement. The service, equipment or supply cannot be procured prior to the first day of the 30-calendar day retroactive date. The beneficiary or the primary caregiver shall agree to and sign and date the service plan acknowledging changes for CAP/DA provision.
Note: The items listed above as exclusion for retroactive approval, may be considered for urgent approval based on necessary need. The POC must be submitted into the CAP Business System along with supporting documentation.

per_question.question: Is there a maximum earned income limit for people on HCWD (Health Coverage for Workers with Disabilities), and what premiums apply?
per_question.agent_answer:
**No—HCWD does not set a maximum *earned-income* limit.** The eligibility ceiling is instead for **unearned income**: a person is not eligible if their unearned income is over **150% of the federal poverty level (FPL)**. Countable income, after applicable exclusions, determines whether cost sharing applies. [Policy MA-2180 § F. Income](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2180-HCWD-ADA-Approval.pdf)

### HCWD fees and premiums

- **Countable income at or below 150% FPL:** no HCWD cost sharing other than any applicable co-payments. [Policy MA-2180 § F. Income](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2180-HCWD-ADA-Approval.pdf)
- **Countable income above 150% FPL:** a **$50 enrollment fee** is due for each 12-month certification period. [Policy MA-2180 § V.A. Enrollment Fee](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2180-HCWD-ADA-Approval.pdf)
- **Countable monthly income above 200% FPL:** the person also owes a **monthly premium**, which rises by income band. [Policy MA-2180 § V.B. Premiums](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2180-HCWD-ADA-Approval.pdf)
- **Above 450% FPL:** the person owes the **full (100%) premium**. [Policy MA-2180 § V.B. Premiums](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2180-HCWD-ADA-Approval.pdf)
- The currently surfaced premium chart lists monthly premiums of **$196–$352 for an individual** and **$265–$476 for a couple** from 201% through 450% FPL; at 451% FPL and above, it lists **$875 per month** for either an individual or couple. [Policy MA-2180 § V.B. Premiums](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2180-HCWD-ADA-Approval.pdf)
- Members of federally recognized Native American tribes and Alaska Natives are exempt from HCWD cost sharing, including both enrollment fees and premiums. [Policy MA-2180 § V.A. Enrollment Fee](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2180-HCWD-ADA-Approval.pdf)

NC Medicaid’s most recent HCWD change notice revised the policy and states that the HCWD premium chart became effective **April 1, 2026**. [Policy MA-2180 Change Notice 05-26](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/CN_05-26.docx.pdf)

The premium table with specific dollar amounts is directly supported by the Evidence (MA-2180 Section B. Premiums). The note about Native American/Alaska Native exemptions is supported by evidence. The April 1, 2026 effective date for the premium chart is supported by the Change Notice 05-26 evidence. All claims are grounded in the evidence blocks. Citations are precise, referencing specific policy sections (MA-2180 § F. Income, § V.A. Enrollment Fee, § V.B. Premiums) and the Change Notice 05-26.

ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-2180:url-08aa92cd33e7:_s15
Title: F. Income
Policy: MA-2180
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)

Content:
HCWD has varying income limits that will determine eligibility and/or cost sharing. These limits are:
Those who have unearned incomes greater than 150% of FPL are not eligible for HCWD.
Those whose total countable income is equal to or less than 150% of FPL have no cost sharing (other than applicable co-payments).
Those whose total countable income is greater than 150% of FPL must pay a $50 annual enrollment fee (see IV. G.).
Those whose total countable monthly income exceeds 200% of FPL must pay a monthly premium in addition to the enrollment fee.  The monthly premium increases as income increases until countable income exceeds 450% of FPL, at which point these individuals must pay a full premium (see IV.H. below). Because countable income determines whether the individual is subject to cost-sharing and the amount thereof, countable income must be determined and all applicable exclusions applied.
Note: These individuals are likely to have work expense exclusions for the blind and impairment-related work expense exclusions for the disabled.

Title: I. Premiums

Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)

Content:
Individuals with countable income above 200% of FPL must pay a monthly premium in addition to an enrollment fee of $50 per year.  The premiums increase with income range until income exceeds 450% of FPL, at which point a 100% premium is due. The 100% premium is based upon the average claims paid for an individual receiving Medicaid and may change yearly.
The income ranges and associated premiums are found in the following chart:

|:------------------------|:------------------------------|------------------:|:---------------------------|------------------:|
| 0-150%                  | $0 - 1,957                    |                 0 | $0 - 2,644                 |                 0 |
| 151-200%                | $1,957.01 - 2,609             |                 0 | $2,644.01 - 3,525          |                 0 |
| 201-250%                | $2,609.01 - 3,261             |               196 | $3,525.01 - 4,407          |               265 |
| 251-300%                | $3,261.01 - 3,913             |               235 | $4,407.01 - 5,288          |               318 |
| 301-350%                | $3,913.01 - 4,565             |               274 | $5,288.01 - 6,169          |               370 |
| 351-400%                | $4,565.01 - 5,217             |               313 | $6,169.01 - 7,050          |               423 |
| 401-450%                | $5,217.01 - 5,869             |               352 | $7,050.01 - 7,932          |               476 |
| 451and above            | $5,869.01 and up              |               875 | $7,932.01 and up           |               875 |

ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-2180:url-08aa92cd33e7:_s17
Title: H. Enrollment Fee
Policy: MA-2180
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)

Content:
All individuals with total monthly countable income above 150% of the federal poverty level must pay a $50 enrollment fee for each twelve month certification period.  The enrollment fee is collected by the county and retained to offset administrative expenses.  Do not charge an enrollment fee for the retroactive month(s) when an a/b receives retroactive coverage.  If a premium is due (see II.C. below), the county must mail the enrollment fee notice with the premium invoice.

ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-2180:url-c2175ac9b51d:_s17
Title: F.  Income
Policy: MA-2180
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2180-HCWD-ADA-Approval.pdf)

Content:
HCWD has varying income limits that determine eligibility and/or cost sharing. These limits are:
Those who have unearned incomes greater than 150% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL) are not eligible for HCWD.
Those whose total countable income is equal to or less than 150% of FPL have no cost sharing (other than applicable co-payments).
Those whose total countable income is greater than 150% of FPL must pay a $50 annual enrollment fee.
Those whose total countable monthly income exceeds 200% of FPL must pay a monthly premium in addition to the enrollment fee.  The monthly premium increases as income increases until countable income exceeds 450% of FPL, at which point the applicant/ beneficiary (a/b) must pay a full premium. The countable income determines whether the a/b is subject to cost-sharing and the amount thereof, countable income must be determined and all applicable exclusions applied.
Refer to MA-2252, Non- MAGI Medicaid Income/Reserve Limits chart.
Note: The a/b is to have work expense exclusions for the blind and impairment-related work expense exclusions for the disabled.
